content: 1. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of sofpironium topical by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Concomitant use of sofpironium with strong CYP2D6 inhibitors may lead to increased sofpironium levels and adverse effects. Monitor closely. 2. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of solifenacin by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Solifenacin and lopinavir both prolong the QTc interval, and lopinavir also increases solifenacin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 3. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of sonidegib by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Lopinavir also increases sonidegib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration of sonidegib with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 4. Sorafenib and lopinavir both prolong the QTc interval. Ritonavir increases sorafenib levels by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Lopinavir also increases sorafenib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. 5. Ritonavir decreases the levels or effects of sotagliflozin by inducing glucuronidation via UGT1A9, which is a major metabolic pathway for sotagliflozin. Coadministration with UGT1A9 inducers may reduce sotagliflozin exposure and efficacy. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 6. Sotorasib decreases ritonavir levels by inducing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, refer to the prescribing information for dosage adjustments. 7. Lopinavir and sparsentan increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, interrupt sparsentan treatment and consider dose titration when resuming. 8. St. John’s Wort decreases ritonavir levels by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. St. John’s Wort is contraindicated with ritonavir or lopinavir due to significant reductions in drug levels. 9. Stiripentol is a CYP3A4 inhibitor and inducer. It increases ritonavir levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Monitor closely. Ritonavir also increases stiripentol levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 10. Ritonavir increases streptomycin levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Ritonavir and lopinavir increase sufentanil levels by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase sufentanil plasma concentrations, leading to prolonged adverse effects, including potentially fatal respiratory depression. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 12. Ritonavir increases sulbactam levels by inhibiting OATP1-mediated active secretion, which is a significant clearance pathway. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 13. Ritonavir increases sunitinib levels by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Sunitinib and lopinavir both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 14. Ritonavir and lopinavir increase suvorexant levels by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Suvorexant is not recommended with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 15. Ritonavir increases tacrolimus levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Tacrolimus and lopinavir both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 16. Ritonavir and lopinavir increase tadalafil levels by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Stop tadalafil at least 24 hours before initiating protease inhibitors (PIs) and restart 7 days after PI initiation at a reduced dose, increasing based on tolerability. 17. Ritonavir increases talazoparib levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Talazoparib is a P-glycoprotein substrate, and coadministration with P-glycoprotein inhibitors may increase systemic exposure. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Ritonavir increases tamoxifen levels by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. CYP3A4 inhibition decreases tamoxifen metabolism to its active metabolite, N-desmethyl tamoxifen. 19. Ritonavir and lopinavir increase tamsulosin levels by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 20. Ritonavir and lopinavir increase tasimelteon levels by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Ritonavir decreases tazemetostat levels by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Lopinavir increases tazemetostat levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 22. Tecovirimat decreases ritonavir and lopinavir levels by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Tecovirimat is a weak CYP3A4 inducer. Monitor sensitive CYP3A4 substrates for effectiveness if coadministered. 23. Ritonavir and lopinavir increase temsirolimus levels by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 24. Ritonavir increases teniposide levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Ritonavir increases tenofovir DF levels by decreasing elimination. Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Tepotinib increases ritonavir levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the P-glycoprotein substrate dosage as recommended. 27. Ritonavir increases terbinafine levels by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Lopinavir also increases terbinafine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Ritonavir increases tetrabenazine levels by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Tetrabenazine and lopinavir both prolong the QTc interval. 29. Ritonavir and lopinavir increase tezacaftor levels by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust tezacaftor dosage if coadministered with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. Monitor closely. 30. Ritonavir increases theophylline levels by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Ritonavir increases thioridazine levels by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 32. Ritonavir and lopinavir increase tiagabine levels by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 33. Ritonavir and lopinavir increase ticagrelor levels by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid use with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Monitor closely. 34. Ritonavir and lopinavir increase timolol levels by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Increased risk of hypotension, bradycardia, AV block, and prolonged PR interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Tinidazole increases lopinavir and ritonavir toxicity by inhibiting aldehyde dehydrogenase. Tinidazole also increases lopinavir levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Contraindicated. 36. Tipranavir increases lopinavir levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, while lopinavir increases tipranavir levels. Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 37. Ritonavir increases tisotumab vedotin levels by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Its active metabolite (MMAE) is a CYP3A4 substrate. Use caution and monitor closely.
